html:
SMTO-WEB-0051 — This PDF is too big for SMTO to download

GUID: a27db80b-fb92-5976-8854-7c560c3a809c
Slug: web-document-too-large
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The PDF is larger than SMTO allows for one downloaded file (at most 64 MB, or less if your administrator set a lower limit). SMTO stopped the download and didn't keep a partial copy.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look for a smaller version of the document, such as a single chapter, a summary or a web page version, and send SMTO that link. A smaller file fits under the download limit, so SMTO can read it in full.
  2. If you have the PDF yourself, save just the pages you need as a new PDF and attach it to your message. Sending only the useful pages keeps the file small enough to use.
  3. Tell SMTO which section or pages matter in your message. Knowing the part you need helps SMTO look for a smaller source covering it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's activity shows the smaller document downloaded, and its answer quotes pages from it.

If it still fails

  • If a PDF well under 64 MB is still refused, select Copy error details and ask the person who manages SMTO whether this server's file size limit was set lower. Don't treat a cut-off copy as the full document.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PDF acquisition stopped because the declared, received or decompressed size exceeded the smallest applicable limit: the PDF limit (64 MiB), the per-file artifact limit or the per-run artifact limit.

What this means

  • PDF acquisition exceeds the minimum applicable Web, artifact-file or artifact-run byte ceiling in declared, wire or decoded size. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • PDF acquisition exceeds the minimum applicable Web, artifact-file or artifact-run byte ceiling in declared, wire or decoded size.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare declared and observed byte counts with the effective minimum ceiling.

How to fix it

  • web/documents.acquire() aborts when Content-Length, wire bytes or decoded bytes exceed min(gateway_core.pdf.contract.MAX_FILE = 64 MiB, AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_FILE_BYTES, AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_RUN_BYTES). The 64 MiB PDF ceiling is fixed; raising the AOR_ARTIFACT_* limits only helps when they are set below it. Otherwise use a smaller document or section; never disable the bound or present a truncated PDF as complete.
  • Use a smaller document or an authoritative section. The Web, artifact and PDF byte ceilings all apply.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized smaller document completes inside all applicable bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the document size bound or present a truncated PDF as complete.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
